title: Create a homebrew distro for the new Rust version of Pplr
objective: Make Homebrew the way Pplr reaches a machine. `brew install matthewsinclair/pplr/pplr` installs a source-built formula, rendered by devbin's formula tool into the tap `matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr`. Releases are cut by devbin 0.1.19's release core, with gates run locally, on the kovacs leg and in CI. pplr follows devbin's dev/opt/brew contract (T1 to T10). The thread ends with rhadamanth running brew's pplr at 2.0.0.

related.note: ST0002 ships ST0001's binary through Homebrew; the install layout is their seam (ST0001 WP02, ST0002 WP01); the release waits on ST0001 WP13

wps.title: Release and install design for pplr
wps.objective: Settle how pplr is installed and released, item by item against devbin's dev/opt/brew contract, and agree the install layout with ST0001 WP02.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- Confirm or amend this thread's design: the T1 to T10 table and decisions E1 to E8.
- **Settle the layout** with ST0001 WP02:
  - the tree root, `bin/pplr`, `bin/pplr-contacts` and the manifest path;
  - the runtime-set function and its inputs (cargo's dep-info plus the sidecar source).
- **Settle the signing details**, with Intent's `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` and its release as the worked example:
  - each binary's identifier and designated requirement;
  - where the notary credentials come from;
  - the order of build, sign, notarise, attach and publish under devbin's release core.
- **Confirm the asset targets** (E1), or bring evidence to drop one.

**Criteria**: AC-01.1.

**Not in scope**: building anything. This WP decides; WP02 to WP07 build.

wps.title: devbin release core and CI candidates
wps.objective: Configure devbin's release core and formula tool for pplr, and make CI fire on release candidates.

wps.title: Install, manifest, tree identity, version line and use
wps.objective: Give the binary the dev/opt/brew verbs, with their doctor rows: `install`, the manifest, the tree function, the version line and `use`.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **T2**: `pplr install [--prefix <dir>] [--force] [--managed-by brew]`.
  - It publishes only from a dev tree, and refuses a dirty runtime set.
  - It replaces a prefix only with `--force`, and only when the manifest says pplr wrote that prefix.
- **T3**: the manifest at `<root>/.pplr-install`. Its header carries `tool`, `version`, `source_commit` and `managed_by`. Its body has one `shasum -a 256 -c` line per runtime file, sorted with `LC_ALL=C`.
- **T4**: one function names the tree. The version line is `pplr <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty])`, built from stamps taken at build time:
  - the commit;
  - dirtiness, measured over cargo's dep-info plus the sidecar source;
  - an optional provenance word.
- **T5**: `pplr use [dev|opt|brew]`.
  - The link set is `pplr` alone, in `~/.local/bin`.
  - It refuses a missing tree, and refuses `use brew` when no brew copy would answer.
  - It runs the shadow check.
- **Doctor rows** for the tree, manifest drift and the shadow check. These are added to ST0001 WP12's doctor.
- **Tests** go in `tests/cli.rs`, using the `Sandbox` with HOME and PATH redirected and a fake brew prefix.

**Criteria**: AC-03.1 to AC-03.3.

**Depends on**: ST0001 WP02 and this thread's WP01.

wps.title: Assets formula, tap and tap CI
wps.objective: Write the `assets` formula template, put the tap in shape, and add the tap's CI.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **`packaging/homebrew/pplr.rb`**, in devbin's `assets` mode, after Intent's formula:
  - `@@VERSION@@`, one `@@SHA256:<asset>@@` per target, and `@@INSTALL@@`/`@@FINISH@@`. No redundant top-level `version`.
  - The macOS assets hold the signed `pplr` and `pplr-contacts`; the Linux assets hold `pplr`.
  - `install` lays the binaries out in `libexec` with mode 0755, writes the T3 manifest with `managed_by: brew`, runs `codesign --verify --strict -R <requirement>` on each macOS binary, and links `pplr` into `bin`.
  - The caveats name `pplr use`, the data root, and the Contacts grant.
  - `test do` verifies the signatures again and runs the version line.
- **Rendering**: `bin/devbin formula render <tag> <out>` renders the template, and the render passes `brew style` and `brew audit --strict`.
- **The tap**, `matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr`, which hv created:
  - correct its description to "Homebrew tap for pplr" (`gh repo edit matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr --description "Homebrew tap for pplr"`), with hv's approval;
  - add a `test.yml` adapted from homebrew-ccusage's, running on macOS and Ubuntu.

**Criteria**: AC-04.1 and AC-04.2.

**Depends on**: WP02, WP03 and WP07.

wps.title: Walking skeleton through a scratch tap
wps.objective: Prove the whole path early, before any real release. Install a build of the scaffold from a locally rendered formula in a scratch tap, and prove T10's three trees.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- In a scratch clone, eg under `~/Devel/scratch/`:
  - render the formula for a scratch tag;
  - install from a local tap;
  - run the version line, doctor and `brew test`;
  - then `pplr use dev`, `use opt` and `use brew`, each followed by the version line, doctor and the shadow check.
- Prefix every brew probe with `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`.
- Nothing is tagged or pushed on the real repository, and the real tap is not written (E8).
- Record the commands and their output on this thread.

**Criteria**: AC-05.1.

**Depends on**: WP04. The binary needs only ST0001 WP02's scaffold plus WP03's verbs; no ported commands.

wps.title: Release 2.0.0 and move rhadamanth to brew
wps.objective: Once ST0001 is done, cut 2.0.0 through devbin's release core, publish the formula, and move rhadamanth onto brew's pplr.

wps.title: Developer ID signing and notarisation
wps.objective: Sign and notarise every macOS binary pplr ships with hv's Geodica Developer ID, through a signer that is project code, so that every release build is signed and checkable.
wps.body:
**Scope**

- **The signer**: `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`, in bash or zsh, ported from Intent's (which was ported from Lamplight's). No Python, so Ccusage's `tools/sign-macos` is out. It uses "Developer ID Application: Geodica Pty Ltd (76BQL8L47U)", the hardened runtime, a secure timestamp and the identifiers WP01 settles.
- **What it signs**:
  - `pplr`;
  - `pplr-contacts`;
  - the `Pplr Links.app` that `pplr handler --install` builds, which ST0001 WP08 calls this step for in place of `codesign --sign -`.
- **Notarisation** with `notarytool`, using a keychain profile on rhadamanth. A bare binary is notarised but never stapled, as in Intent.
- **Checks**: `codesign --verify --strict -R <requirement>` and `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature`, as Intent does. Doctor reports the same verdict for the running tree on macOS.
- **Where it runs**: on rhadamanth only, never on CI. It is wired into the release so the macOS assets are signed before `release attach` (E3).
- **Proof on a scratch build**: a signed, notarised build that passes every check. Nothing is published.

**Criteria**: AC-07.1 and AC-07.2.

**Depends on**: WP01, and ST0001 WP09 for the sidecar.

criteria.text: From the tap on rhadamanth, `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew install matthewsinclair/pplr/pplr` succeeds, `brew test pplr` passes (including the signature check), and `pplr --version` reads `pplr 2.0.0 (brew, <sha12>)`, naming the release commit.
T10 holds: on rhadamanth, `pplr use dev`, `use opt` and `use brew` each give the right version line, a clean doctor and a passing shadow check, and on a Linux machine brew alone does.
rhadamanth runs brew's pplr, with no link into the old checkout. The user docs name brew alone (T1), and docs/releasing.md covers dev and opt for the maintainer.
The release and install design (E1 to E8, the T1 to T10 table, the install layout) is settled on this thread, with hv's answers to its open questions recorded.
`bin/devbin release check` and `bin/devbin doctor` pass with the release and formula config, and tests.yml fires on candidate/** and runs the cargo gates and the bats suite on macOS and Linux.
tools/lock-sync (zsh) rewrites Cargo.lock for a version bump and prints Cargo.lock, and the CHANGELOG opens 2.0.0 as `## [2.0.0] - unreleased`.
`pplr install` publishes only from a clean dev tree and writes the T3 manifest, and it refuses an existing prefix without --force, or a prefix another tool wrote.
The version line reads `pplr <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty])` in dev, opt and brew, built from stamps taken at build time, with the tree named by the one tree function.

`pplr use dev|opt|brew` moves only the link set {pplr} in ~/.local/bin, and refuses a missing tree or a brew copy that would not answer. Doctor's shadow check fails on a link that is shadowed or split across trees.

packaging/homebrew/pplr.rb is a devbin `assets` template, rendered through `bin/devbin formula render` with nothing typed. The render passes `brew style` and `brew audit --strict`, its install verifies every macOS binary's signature against its designated requirement and writes the T3 manifest, and its test re-verifies the signatures and runs the version line.
The tap matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr is described as "Homebrew tap for pplr", and its CI runs style, audit, install and test on macOS and Ubuntu.
A scaffold build installs from a locally rendered formula in a scratch tap on rhadamanth, T10's three trees are proved, and nothing is tagged or pushed on the real repository.
2.0.0 is cut by `bin/devbin release`. Its gates pass locally, on kovacs and in CI for candidate/v2.0.0, and the formula is published to the tap by `bin/devbin formula publish`.

The Contacts grant holds across upgrades: after a `brew upgrade` or `brew reinstall`, `pplr sync --check` from the keg reads the live store with no new permission prompt, and any first-use prompt for the signed sidecar is recorded.

Every macOS binary pplr ships (`pplr`, `pplr-contacts` and the `Pplr Links.app` from `pplr handler`) is signed with Developer ID Application: Geodica Pty Ltd (76BQL8L47U), with the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp, and passes `codesign --verify --strict -R <requirement>` and `spctl`.

The signer is project code in bash or zsh (`bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`, no Python). It runs on rhadamanth only, notarises every release build with `notarytool`, and the release cannot attach an unsigned macOS asset.

attachments.text:
# ST0002 design: Pplr through Homebrew Design record by vc, 2026-11-02, revised the same day with hv's answers. It draws on a survey of Cldr, Ccusage, Intent and devbin 0.1.19, dc's boot findings and cc's survey. ST0001 builds the binary; this thread makes Homebrew the way it reaches a machine. ST0001's recon (`recon.md` on ST0001) carries the Pplr facts this rests on. ## 1. Rulings (hv, 2026-11-02) 1. **Everything is signed** with hv's Geodica Developer ID, whether or not anything needs it today. For pplr that is every macOS binary it ships: `pplr`, the `pplr-contacts` sidecar, and the `Pplr Links.app` that `pplr handler` builds. 2. **dc runs the release cut, with hv's approval.** 3. **The tap exists**: `matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr`, created by hv, empty. Its description reads "Homebrew tap for cldr" and needs correcting. 4. **kovacs is ready** as the Linux leg. ## 2. The contract **Pplr joins devbin's dev/opt/brew contract**, `~/Devel/prj/Devbin/docs/dev-opt-brew.md` (T1 to T10), as Molt, Utilz, Intent and devbin already do. dc proposed it, and devbin's release flow expects it. **Intent is the worked example to follow**: it ships signed, notarised bare binaries through an `assets` formula under the same contract. Applied to pplr: | Item | What it means for pplr | | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | T1 | **Three trees**: dev (the checkout), opt (a prefix the maintainer names, with no default) and brew (`$(brew --prefix)/opt/pplr/libexec`).
A tree holds `/bin/pplr`, `/bin/pplr-contacts` on macOS, and the manifest. Templates, icons and the README are inside the binary (ST0001 D6).
The binary finds its root from its resolved path. One function lists the runtime set, and install and doctor both read it. | | T2 | **`pplr install [--prefix ] [--force]` publishes from dev to opt only.**
It refuses a dirty runtime set: the build inputs from cargo's dep-info, plus the sidecar source.
It replaces a prefix only with `--force`, and only when the manifest says pplr wrote it.
`install` never writes the brew tree: as T2 allows for signed assets, the formula lays the signed binaries out and writes the manifest itself. | | T3 | **The manifest is `/.pplr-install`.** Its header carries `# tool`, `# version`, `# source_commit` (the full sha the binaries were built from) and `# managed_by`. Its body has one `shasum -a 256 -c` line per runtime file, sorted with `LC_ALL=C sort`. In opt and brew, doctor checks it and names each drifted file. | | T4 | **One function names the tree**: brew, opt, dev or unknown.
`pplr --version` and `pplr version` print `pplr (, [+dirty])`. The commit and the dirtiness are stamped into the binary at build time, and one provenance word (`release` or `dev`) may follow the closing parenthesis.
Doctor prints the same line. | | T5 | **`pplr use [dev\|opt\|brew]`.** The link set is `pplr` alone, in `~/.local/bin`; the sidecar is never linked. `use brew` removes the link, and refuses when no brew copy would answer. Doctor runs the shadow check. | | T6 | **No upgrade verb.** The docs give the steps per tree: in dev, `git pull` and build; in opt, `pplr install --force` from dev; in brew, `brew upgrade pplr`. | | T7 | **pplr has no test or lint verbs** (devbin's `test` and `check` are the project's), so it has nothing to refuse. Recorded, not built. | | T8 | **The formula is rendered, never typed**: from `packaging/homebrew/pplr.rb` by `bin/devbin formula`, in `assets` mode, taking the version and each asset's sha256 from the release.
`install` lays the binaries out in `libexec` with mode 0755, writes the T3 manifest with `managed_by: brew`, verifies each signature against its designated requirement, and links `pplr` into `bin`.
The caveats name `pplr use`. `test do` verifies the signatures again and runs the version line. | | T9 | devbin only: not applicable. | | T10 | **The proof**: on rhadamanth, `use dev`, `use opt` and `use brew`, each followed by the version line, doctor and the shadow check; on kovacs, brew alone. Every brew probe is prefixed with `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`. | ## 3. Decisions | ID | Decision | Why | | --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | E1 | **An `assets` formula** (devbin's `formula: mode: assets`, as Intent's): release assets per target, each with its sha256 taken from the release's `SHA256SUMS`.
The macOS assets hold `pplr` and `pplr-contacts`, both signed and notarised. The Linux assets hold `pplr` alone.
The targets: aarch64 and x86_64 on macOS, x86_64 and aarch64 on Linux, as Ccusage ships, unless WP01 finds a reason to drop one. | Ruling 1. A keg cannot build signed binaries from source, so the formula installs what was signed. | | E2 | **Developer ID signing and notarisation for every macOS binary**, with "Developer ID Application: Geodica Pty Ltd (76BQL8L47U)":
- each binary has a fixed identifier (eg `com.geodica.pplr`, `com.geodica.pplr-contacts`; WP01 settles them);
- the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp;
- notarised with `notarytool`;
- verified with `codesign --verify --strict -R ` and `spctl`, as Intent does.
Signing runs on rhadamanth, where the identity lives, never on CI. The signer is project code in bash or zsh: `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`, ported from Intent's, which was itself ported from Lamplight's. Ccusage's signer is Python, which rules it out. | Ruling 1. A stable designated requirement also keeps the Contacts and Automation grants stable across upgrades. | | E3 | **devbin's release core cuts every release** (devbin `^0.1.19`):
- `release.repo: matthewsinclair/pplr`;
- `remotes: [local, upstream]`, the Dropbox bare repo then GitHub, which is devbin's standard shape;
- the gates `check all`, `test all` and `doctor`, the kovacs leg, and CI on `candidate/`;
- the notes kind `changelog`;
- the release assets built by a CI workflow (`assets.workflow`), with the macOS ones signed and notarised by `bin/devbin macos`, then attached by `bin/devbin release attach --from `, which writes `SHA256SUMS`;
- `after: [bin/devbin formula publish]`.
WP01 settles the exact order of build, sign, attach and publish, following Intent's release. | One release sequence shared with every devbin project, not a bespoke `tools/release`. | | E4 | **The version lives in `Cargo.toml`** (`version_from: Cargo.toml`). The release owns `Cargo.lock` through a `derived:` step, `tools/lock-sync`: zsh, modelled on Gtools', which rewrites the lock and prints `Cargo.lock`. | devbin refuses `Cargo.lock` as a sidecar, and ST0001 D7 makes `Cargo.toml` the only version source. | | E5 | **The tap is `matthewsinclair/homebrew-pplr`**, with its description corrected to "Homebrew tap for pplr". It carries a `test.yml` adapted from homebrew-ccusage's, which on macOS and Ubuntu runs `brew style`, `brew audit --strict`, `brew install`, and `brew test` with the signature check. | Every tool's tap follows this convention, and devbin's formula tool derives the tap's name from it by default. | | E6 | **CI is `.github/workflows/tests.yml`**, firing on `main` and `candidate/**` and hardened in house style: `permissions: contents: read`, actions pinned by sha, `persist-credentials: false`, `fail-fast: false`, timeouts. It runs the cargo gates and the bats suite against the Rust binary on macOS and Linux. A separate workflow builds the release assets from the tag. | devbin's pre-flight refuses a cut unless pushing `candidate/` starts `ci.workflow` (default `tests.yml`). ST0001 WP02 builds `tests.yml`; this thread adds the candidate trigger and the asset build. | | E7 | **The CHANGELOG opens each release as `## [X.Y.Z] - unreleased`**, starting with 2.0.0. | devbin's default `changelog` notes kind reads that heading, not `## [Unreleased]`. | | E8 | **Outward-facing steps happen only in WP06**: no tag, push, release, notarisation of a release build, or tap write before then. In WP06, dc runs each outward step with hv's approval. Earlier work proves the path on a scratch clone and a scratch tap. | These steps are outward-facing and hard to reverse. | ## 4. What the binary must provide ST0001 builds the commands. This thread needs these from the binary, built in WP03 on ST0001's scaffold: - the resolved root and the tree function (T1, T4); - `install` and `use` (T2, T5), and the manifest (T3); - the version line, with the build commit and dirtiness stamped in (T4); - doctor rows for the tree, the manifest, the shadow check and, on macOS, each binary's signature, added to ST0001's doctor; - `handler --install` naming the opt link under brew (ST0001 WP08), and the app it builds signed with the Geodica identity instead of today's ad-hoc `codesign --sign -` (WP07 provides the signing step); - `help --details` from the embedded README (ST0001 D6). ## 5. Migration on rhadamanth - Today `~/.local/bin/pplr` links to the checkout's bash dispatcher. After 2.0.0, `brew install` followed by `pplr use brew` removes that link, and doctor's shadow check confirms brew answers. - `setup.sh` and `.env.example` go in ST0001 WP13. Any of these in the user's shell configuration lives in Molt-matts, not here: `PPLR_ROOT`, `PPLR_BIN_DIR`, or the checkout's `bin/` on `PATH`. Doctor names it, and Molt-matts makes the fix. - The Contacts grant moves from the terminal-run legacy engine to the signed `pplr-contacts`. WP06 records whether macOS asks again, and confirms that a `brew upgrade` does not. - None of this touches the People tree. ## 6. Open questions for hv None. The targets in E1 stand unless WP01 brings evidence to drop one.
